meta.title: Steps to Turn Off System Integrity Protection (SIP)

segments.label: Check SIP and the local administrator
Prepare and boot into macOS Recovery
Turn off SIP and clean up

messages.label: 1. Ask Pomme to turn off SIP
2. Save the VM's starting run state
If SIP is already off, save no change and skip to step 17
4. Verify a local administrator, or create the pomme user
messages.note: Pomme uses an existing authorized administrator when possible. It creates the pomme account only after proving the VM is new and receiving confirmation or --force.

messages.label: 5. On a new VM, enable automatic login
6. On a new VM, finish setup and open the desktop as pomme
7. Save the plan and prepare Pomme's signed Recovery helper
8. Shut down the VM and boot into macOS Recovery
9. Open Terminal in Recovery
messages.note: Reviewed Tahoe 25G72 route: Right twice, Return twice, Control-F2, Right four times, Down, Shift-Command-T. Guarded experimental 25G83 route: Right twice, Return twice, Shift-Command-T. For each key, Pomme checks two matching screen images, sends and confirms one key, then checks two matching images again.

messages.label: 10. Start the helper and verify Recovery, root, and the Mac disk
messages.note: root is macOS's highest-privilege system account. The helper must match this request and this VM before it can continue.

messages.label: 11. Run csrutil disable with the administrator password
12. Run csrutil status and confirm SIP is off
14. Remove temporary files and confirm cleanup
messages.note: Disconnect the temporary share and stop the Recovery helper. If any cleanup check fails, Pomme leaves the VM stopped.

messages.label: 16. Run csrutil status again and confirm SIP is off
17. Return the VM to its starting state and report success
